name: Container freight
summary: Drewry container index fell 2% to $4,305 per 40ft on 12 Nov, still above the $4,000 Alert line
state: Drewry's World Container Index fell 2% to $4,305 per 40ft container on 12 Nov, down from $4,389 on 5 Nov and $4,434 on 1 Oct, but still above the $4,000 Alert line (Drewry). Shanghai–New York fell 3% to $9,020, its lowest since August, while Shanghai congestion rose to 49 hours from 36. Drewry expects transpacific rates to fall further next week.
for_you: Importers and retailers relying on Asian goods are exposed to high shipping costs, which can feed through to shelf prices with a lag.
basis_detail: Drewry World Container Index / Freightos Baltic Index
basis_by: Drewry World Container Index / Freightos Baltic Index
why: Container rates feed through to goods prices months later; spikes are an early inflation and supply-chain warning.
drivers: Chokepoint diversions, capacity, demand, port congestion, tariffs front-running.

rubric.normal: Drewry World Container Index < $2,500/FEU and 1-month change < +30%.
